bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "Central Yukon Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan".
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) relating to the Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan (RMP) for Alaska’s Central Yukon planning area and issued on November 12, 2024. By way of background, an RMP guides the management of lands administered by the BLM. This Central Yukon RMP modified the prior RMP for the area, including by designating 21 areas of critical environmental concern or research natural areas, encompassing approximately 3,611,000 acres.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify a Bureau of Land Management rule issued in November 2024 that governs how approximately 3.6 million acres of federal land in Alaska's Central Yukon area are managed. The BLM rule designated 21 areas as critical environmental concern or research natural areas. If passed, the resolution would cancel that rule and prevent it from taking effect.

industries.rationale: Designation of critical environmental concern areas on federal land typically restricts oil and gas leasing and extraction activities.
Resource management plan designations directly affect mineral extraction rights and mining operations on federal lands.
Environmental and conservation organizations have direct stakes in land-use designations and protected-area classifications.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the rule submitted by the federal land agency relating to the Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan for Alaska’s Central Yukon planning area and issued on November 12, 2024.
plain.whoItTouches: People who live near or work on federal land.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what may be done with that land. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
